body: We should also add a remark here that instances of this class (and any of its subclasses), should only ever be interacted with from the rendering thread.

So light storage, as with the other storage classes, are part of the core rendering system. You can just return this through `https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/rendering_server_globals.cpp`.
It can then be cast to (`RendererRD::`)`LightStorage` in GDScript.

This also means this function does not need to be virtual, and we don't need the overridden function in `RenderDataRD`.

Just for others, this is the only question mark in this solution.

The classes in the rendering engine are namespaced (`RendererRD::` and `GLES3::`) and thus do not have unique names. Now that we're exposing them through `ClassDB` we have a problem if we want to expose both the compatibility and render device storage classes because `ClassDB` doesn't support namespacing (yet).

It is likely that we'll only ever expose the rendering device storage classes. Otherwise we may need to rename the classes after all or talk to the script team about what it will take to add namespace support to `ClassDB`.

@BastiaanOlij I followed your advice and got rid of the LightStorage class usage in RenderDataRD class, I also removed the implementation of the method from there and added it in the base class using RenderingServerGlobals instead. But when you say it doesnt need to be virtual, I guess it should stay virtual because at least RenderDataExtension class is inherited from RenderData and if Im not mistaken it sould be able to override the method in order to add custom behaviour, right?

```suggestion
		RID fb; // When rendering direct.
```

Ok, so they both access the same texture, but `decal_atlas_get_texture` will read the color data in linear color space (or convert the contents to linear when reading), while `decal_atlas_get_texture_srgb` will read the color data in sRGB color space (or convert the contents to sRGB when reading). 

The code you copied here is just the default blank texture we provide when no atlas texture is available. As this is just a 4x4 black texture there is no point in doing color conversion.

The real code can be found in `TextureStorage::update_decal_atlas`. Here we create the real atlas used and you'll find this line of code: `decal_atlas.texture_srgb = RD::get_singleton()->texture_create_shared(rd_view, decal_atlas.texture);`
That creates access to this texture with sRGB conversion.

It shouldn't need to be, also not for `RenderDataExtension`. There can only ever be one instance of the `LightStorage` class and the correct one will be instantiated by the renderer and assigned to the variable in `RenderingServerGlobals`, which is what we're returning. 

From here Godot is more than capable to cast to the correct subclass.
